narrative:
The model predicts an 18% chance that you will fail your final year, which is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this prediction were your number of past class failures, your desire to pursue higher education, and whether you attended nursery school. Past failures had the biggest impact and unfortunately pushed the model toward expecting you to fail. Even though you currently have zero past failures (matching the average of students who passed), the model still sees this history as a warning sign for future performance. Your strong ambition to continue into higher education worked in the opposite direction, pulling the prediction toward passing. Similarly, not having attended nursery school also nudged the outcome slightly toward passing, though this had a smaller effect.

Taken together, these elements created enough concern for the system to flag a risk of failure. To improve your chances, focus on building consistent study habits now, seek extra academic support early if you feel behind, and talk to your teachers about targeted help in any subjects where you have struggled before. Small, steady improvements in your daily routine can make a real difference before the final exams. (218 words)
